_meta.note: Guided pre-purchase checklist for a buyer with no tools beyond a phone, flashlight, paper towel and (optional) a cheap OBD2 Bluetooth reader. Drafted by AI from general automotive knowledge — have a mechanic review before launch. The app never says a car is safe; it points out risks and always recommends a professional pre-purchase inspection (PPI) for a purchase.

severity.info: Good to know, rarely affects price
severity.minor: Small cost or wear item; use for negotiation
severity.major: Expensive repair likely; negotiate hard or get a PPI
severity.critical: Deal-breaker or safety/legal problem until proven otherwise

items.title: VIN matches everywhere
how_to_check: Find the VIN at the bottom of the windshield (driver side) and on the driver door jamb sticker.
Compare both with the title and the listing.

items.title: Title is clean and in the seller's name
how_to_check: Ask to see the title.
Check the name matches the seller's ID.
Look for brands like Salvage, Rebuilt, Flood, Lemon, Junk.
bad_signs: Seller isn't on the title ('selling for a friend')
Lien listed without a payoff plan
No title ('it's coming in the mail')

items.title: Service records exist
how_to_check: Ask for receipts or a service history printout.
Look for regular oil changes and major services at the right mileage (e.g., timing belt).
bad_signs: No records at all on a high-mileage car
Major service due soon with no proof it was done

items.title: Timing belt done if due
how_to_check: Ask whether the engine has a timing belt or chain (the app shows a reminder if known).
If belt: check records for replacement at the interval (often 60k–105k miles).
bad_signs: Belt overdue with no proof of replacement

items.title: Mileage looks plausible
how_to_check: Compare odometer with records, inspection stickers and listing.
Compare wear on the steering wheel, pedals and driver seat with the mileage.
bad_signs: Heavy pedal/seat wear on 'low mileage' car

items.title: Open recalls fixed
how_to_check: Review the recalls the app found for this model.
Ask the seller or a dealer whether each recall was completed (recall repairs are free at dealers).

items.title: All keys included
how_to_check: Ask how many keys/fobs come with the car and test each.
bad_signs: Only one key (replacement fobs can cost $200–$500)

items.title: Even panel gaps
how_to_check: Walk around and look at the gaps between hood, fenders, doors and trunk.
Gaps should be even on both sides.

items.title: Paint color and texture match
how_to_check: Look along the car in daylight at an angle.
Compare color and 'orange peel' texture panel to panel.
Look for overspray on rubber seals, trim and in door jambs.
bad_signs: Slightly different shade on one panel

items.title: Dents and scratches
how_to_check: Walk around slowly; photograph each mark.

items.title: Body rust
how_to_check: Check wheel arches, rocker panels (below doors), door bottoms and trunk lid edges.
Press gently near bubbles.

items.title: Windshield and glass
how_to_check: Look for chips and cracks, especially in the driver's view.
Check glass brand markings match on all windows.
bad_signs: One window with a different brand (replaced after damage)

items.title: All lights work
how_to_check: Test headlights (low/high), turn signals, brake lights, reverse, hazards.
Look for moisture inside lenses.

items.title: No flood signs outside
how_to_check: Look for a water line or mud inside headlights, taillights and the trunk spare-tire well.
bad_signs: Silt or mud in spare-tire well
Rust on unpainted bolts in odd places

items.title: Tire tread depth
how_to_check: Insert a penny upside down into the tread (US).
If you can see all of Lincoln's head, tread is under 2/32" — tires are worn out.
Check all four tires and the spare.
bad_signs: Tread at or near the wear bars

items.title: Even tire wear
how_to_check: Compare the inner, middle and outer tread on each front tire.
bad_signs: Inner or outer edge worn more (alignment/suspension issue)

items.title: Tire age and sidewalls
how_to_check: Find the 4-digit DOT date code on the sidewall (week + year, e.g., 2321 = week 23, 2021).
Look for cracks and bulges.

items.title: Wheels not bent or cracked
how_to_check: Look at rim edges for curb rash, bends or cracks.

items.title: Brake discs look healthy
how_to_check: Look through the wheel spokes at the brake discs.
Feel for a lip at the outer edge (when cool).
bad_signs: Heavy rust on the friction surface

items.title: Engine is cold when you arrive
how_to_check: Ask the seller not to start the car before you arrive.
Touch the hood/engine cover: it should be cool.
bad_signs: Engine already warm (can hide starting problems, smoke and noises)

items.title: Oil level and condition
how_to_check: Pull the dipstick, wipe, re-insert, pull again.
Check level between marks; wipe oil on a paper towel.
bad_signs: Milky or foamy oil (possible head gasket)

items.title: Under the oil cap
how_to_check: Remove the oil filler cap (engine off) and look underneath with a flashlight.

items.title: Coolant level and color
how_to_check: NEVER open the radiator cap on a warm engine.
Check the coolant reservoir level and color through the plastic.

items.title: Leaks in the engine bay
how_to_check: Look for wet, dark, dirt-caked areas around the engine and underneath.
A freshly steam-cleaned engine bay is worth asking about.
bad_signs: Drips on the ground under the engine
Suspiciously spotless engine on an old car

items.title: Belts and hoses
how_to_check: Look at the drive belt for cracks.
Squeeze cool rubber hoses: they should feel firm, not mushy or brittle.

items.title: 12V battery
how_to_check: Look for a date sticker on the battery.
Check terminals for white/green corrosion.

items.title: Brake fluid
how_to_check: Check the brake fluid reservoir level and color.

items.title: Transmission fluid (if dipstick)
how_to_check: Many modern cars have no dipstick — skip if so.
If there is one: check with engine running per the cap's instructions; smell it.

items.title: Smell test
how_to_check: Close the doors for a minute, then open and smell.
bad_signs: Musty or mildew smell (water leak or flood)

items.title: Carpets dry, no silt
how_to_check: Press the carpet in all footwells and the trunk.
Lift a floor mat corner; look under seats for rust on seat rails.
bad_signs: Brand-new carpet in an old car

items.title: Warning lights at startup
how_to_check: Turn the key to ON without starting: most warning lights should light up briefly (bulb check).
Start the car: they should all go out within a few seconds.
Take a photo of the dashboard right after starting.
bad_signs: Check engine, airbag, ABS or battery light stays on
Airbag light never lights up at all (bulb may be removed to hide a fault)

items.title: Airbag light behaves normally
how_to_check: Watch the airbag (SRS) light at startup: it should light briefly, then go out.

items.title: A/C and heat
how_to_check: Run the A/C on max: air should be cold within ~1 minute.
Switch to heat once warmed up.
Test all fan speeds and vents.

items.title: Windows, locks, mirrors, screen
how_to_check: Test every window, lock, mirror and seat adjustment.
Test the screen, backup camera, Bluetooth, USB ports and horn.

items.title: Seats and seat belts
how_to_check: Pull each seat belt fully out and let it retract; tug hard to check it locks.
Check seat wear vs mileage.
bad_signs: Very worn driver seat on a low-mileage car

items.title: Roof and sunroof leaks
how_to_check: Look at the headliner for stains, especially around the sunroof and pillars.

items.title: Frame and structure
how_to_check: With a flashlight, look behind the front and rear bumpers and under the trunk floor.
Look for crinkled metal, welds or clamp marks.

items.title: Underbody rust
how_to_check: Look at the floor pans, subframes and brake lines.
Surface rust is normal in snowy states; flaking or holes are not.

items.title: Drips under the car
how_to_check: Look at the ground where the car was parked and under the engine/transmission.
bad_signs: Clear water near A/C is normal

items.title: Exhaust system
how_to_check: Look for rust holes and broken hangers.
Check that the catalytic converter is present (theft is common).
bad_signs: Missing catalytic converter or cut pipes

items.title: CV boots (front wheels)
how_to_check: Look behind the front wheels at the rubber boots on the axles.

items.title: Starts easily, smooth idle
how_to_check: Start the cold engine; listen for the first 30 seconds.
Watch the exhaust at startup.
bad_signs: Knocking or ticking that doesn't fade

items.title: Engine pulls smoothly
how_to_check: Accelerate firmly from a stop and on a merge (safely).

items.title: Smooth shifts
how_to_check: Feel each shift during gentle and firm acceleration.
Shift into Drive and Reverse while stopped: engagement should be quick and soft.
bad_signs: Slipping (revs rise, car doesn't speed up)

items.title: Clutch (manual only)
how_to_check: Note where the clutch bites.
In 3rd/4th gear at low speed, press the gas: revs and speed should rise together.

items.title: Brakes
how_to_check: Brake firmly from ~30 mph on an empty road.
Notice pedal feel and any pulling.

items.title: Steering and alignment
how_to_check: On a straight, flat road, loosen your grip briefly: the car should track straight.
Check the steering wheel is centered.

items.title: Suspension noises
how_to_check: Drive over speed bumps and rough roads with the radio off.
Turn sharply at low speed both ways (e.g., in a parking lot).

items.title: Highway speed check
how_to_check: If safe, drive at 55–70 mph for a few minutes.
bad_signs: Humming that changes with speed (wheel bearing)

items.title: Temperature stays normal
how_to_check: Watch the temperature gauge during the drive and while idling after.

items.title: Driver-assist features
how_to_check: Check cruise control, lane-keep and parking sensors if equipped.
bad_signs: Warnings that a sensor/camera is unavailable

items.title: Look again for leaks and smells
how_to_check: Park on a clean spot for 5 minutes with engine running, then look underneath.
Open the hood and smell.

items.title: No new warning lights
how_to_check: Check the dashboard again after the drive and take a photo.
bad_signs: Any warning light appeared during the drive

items.title: OBD2 scan (optional, ~$20 reader)
how_to_check: Plug a Bluetooth OBD2 reader into the port under the dashboard.
Read stored and pending codes.
Check 'readiness monitors' / 'I/M readiness'.
bad_signs: Several readiness monitors 'not ready' — codes may have been cleared recently to hide a problem

items.title: Hybrid battery behavior
how_to_check: Watch the energy display: the engine should switch off at low speeds and the battery should charge when braking.
Ask for any hybrid battery service records.
bad_signs: Battery gauge jumps between empty and full

items.title: EV battery health
how_to_check: Ask for a battery health (SOH) report from a dealer or app.
Compare the shown range at 100% to the original EPA range.
bad_signs: Range far below original for the age

items.title: Charging works
how_to_check: Plug in (Level 2 or the included cable) and confirm it starts charging.
Check the charge port and cable for damage.

items.title: Diesel smoke and DPF
how_to_check: Watch exhaust under hard acceleration.
Ask about DPF/AdBlue (DEF) warnings and service.
bad_signs: DPF removed ('deleted') — illegal in the US
